# ReqFlow

From customer evidence to prioritized, PM-approved vehicle requirements. A **desktop app for Windows,
macOS and Linux** (Electron), built as a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _AI for Product
Decision Making_.

| Read                                         | For                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md)                     | What we build and why (the product definition)          |
| [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)                       | Challenge digest and rules for every coding agent       |
| [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Stack, layout, processes, IPC API, engine semantics     |
| [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md)   | Parallel work packages and path ownership               |
| [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md)             | Current state, task list per workstream, handoffs       |
| [docs/AGENT_PROMPT.md](docs/AGENT_PROMPT.md) | The prompt that starts a new AI teammate                |
| [docs/decisions/](docs/decisions/)           | Architecture decisions (why Electron, why one TS stack) |
| [context/](context/)                         | Original briefing material                              |

## Setup (once)

Requires Node ≥ 22.13 (see `.nvmrc`) and git. Install **Entire**, which records agent sessions as
checkpoints on each commit:

- macOS / Linux:

  ```bash
  brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire
  ```

- Windows (PowerShell):

  ```powershell
  irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex
  ```

Then, in each clone:

```bash
entire enable --agent claude-code
```

```bash
npm install
```

Optional, dev only: copy `.env.example` to `apps/desktop/.env` and add an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Without
one, the default AI provider is the offline `mock`.

## Daily commands

```bash
npm run dev       # open the app with hot reload
npm run smoke     # build, screenshot every screen to apps/desktop/out/smoke/, check the IPC bridge
npm run check     # typecheck + tests + format check
npm run package   # installer for your OS → apps/desktop/release/
```

The ReqFlow desktop app is running in dev mode on your Mac, and I brought its window to the front. If you don't see it, look for "Electron" in the Dock.

- **What's running:** `npm run dev` in `reqflow/`, which runs `electron-vite dev` for `apps/desktop`. Dependencies and the Electron binary were already installed, so it started right away.
- **Hot reload:** changes to the UI (renderer) show up immediately. Changes to the main process (`src/main/*`) restart the window.
- **AI provider:** there's no `apps/desktop/.env`, so the app uses the offline `mock` AI provider. To use Claude, copy `.env.example` to `apps/desktop/.env` and add an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- **Uncommitted changes:** the app includes the edits you haven't committed yet in `apps/desktop/src/main/`, such as `handlers.ts`, `index.ts` and the new storage and importer files.

The dev server keeps running in the background. Tell me when you want it stopped, or just close the app window.

The ReqFlow app is no longer running. It ran for about 10 minutes and then got a stop signal (exit code 143) from outside. It didn't crash: there's no error before the shutdown.

Something else changed the code just before it stopped. Around 7:14 PM, many files in the checkout changed at once and the app reloaded several times. `main` now points to `9dccb5a`, the merge of PR #7 (the AI Splitter replacement); when I started the app it was at `3caf629`. That looks like a pull or merge, probably from you or another session, which then also stopped the dev server. The other possibility is that you quit the window yourself.

Nothing is running on port 5173 now, so it can restart cleanly. Do you want me to restart `npm run dev` on the new code? If the merge added dependencies, I'll run `npm install` first.
